title: PowerPoint (Desktop): reference SharePoint and OneDrive files when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold for corrections to governance and protection guidance. Microsoft documents general rollout mechanics and protection coverage that the briefing treats as unknown, and the encryption exceptions need to retain the EXTRACT requirement in both cases. The roadmap facts and the Restricted Content Discovery path and command are supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[1].governs; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits discovery of selected SharePoint sites in Copilot and organization-wide search.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.claim: The SharePoint admin center path is Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery on a site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Open PowerShell as an administrator and run the following command:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery leaves existing permissions and direct user access unchanged.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: The row presents Restricted Content Discovery as a general Copilot control not confirmed for Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.
claims.fix: Replace the note in front matter and the rendered table with: 'Applies to organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including tenant-wide content discovery. Existing permissions and direct access are unchanged.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Whether Restricted Content Discovery governs this Copilot file lookup is unconfirmed because its page does not name Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.
claims.fix: Replace the prose applicability caveats with: 'Restricted Content Discovery governs organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including tenant-wide content discovery; it does not change permissions or prevent direct access to content.' Remove the RCD applicability question. Keep testing advice as advice, not as evidence that the general control is unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Copilot and agents cannot access unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions, subject to exceptions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive that are labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions.

claims.claim: The exceptions are a default label extending SharePoint permissions to downloads and a document directly referenced by typing '/'.
claims.quote: There are two exceptions: the label is a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents, or the user references the document directly by typing "/".

claims.claim: The encryption-exception sentence attaches the additional EXTRACT requirement to the direct-reference exception without retaining it for the default-label exception.
claims.quote: In both cases, the user must also have the EXTRACT usage right.
claims.fix: End the exception list after 'typing "/"' and add: 'In both cases, the user must also have the EXTRACT usage right.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A DLP policy for Copilot can prevent summarization of labeled files and emails.
claims.quote: A DLP policy for Copilot can keep Copilot from summarizing labeled files and emails. Copilot can still return a link so the user can open the item outside Copilot.

claims.where: Open questions: DLP for Copilot on Desktop
claims.claim: Whether DLP for Copilot covers this PowerPoint file-processing scenario remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote:
Block files and emails with sensitivity labels from being processed
This feature is available in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork, and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
claims.fix: Remove the DLP applicability question and add this source. Replace it with the factual sentence: 'Microsoft documents sensitivity-label-based DLP blocking of file processing in Copilot in PowerPoint; protected items may still appear in citations, but their content is not used in the response.'
